# Specifies the base image for the build environment. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, well-supported choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during the build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers (GCC/G++), version control (Git),
# networking tools (wget), security certificates, and the OpenMPI library required for parallel execution.
# Cleaning up apt lists reduces the final image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \
    git \
    make \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create and set a temporary working directory for compiling the application and its dependencies.
WORKDIR /tmp/build

# Download, build, and install METIS 4.0.3 from source.
# Use OPTFLAGS instead of CFLAGS. This allows the METIS Makefile to correctly construct
# the full compiler flags, including the necessary include paths, preventing header not found errors.
RUN wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/

# Download, build, and install Hypre 2.28.0 from source.
# FIX: Manually copy the library and all required header files to system paths. The standard
# 'make install' is unreliable and fails to copy all necessary headers, causing downstream build failures.
RUN wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp lib/libHYPRE.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/

# Clone and build the MFEM (Modular Finite Element Methods) library version 4.7 from source.
# Explicitly provide paths to the system-installed Hypre and METIS dependencies,
# as the MFEM Makefile does not automatically detect them in /usr/local.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local

# Clone and build the Laghos application.
# The build is linked against the MFEM library compiled in the previous step.
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    MFEM_DIR=/tmp/build/mfem make -j$(nproc)

# Prepare the final application environment. This includes creating a dedicated app directory,
# copying the Laghos executable to a location on the system's PATH, and moving the necessary
# input data files. The temporary build directory is then removed to keep the final image clean.
RUN mkdir -p /app && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/data/* /app/ && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build

# Set environment variables required for OpenMPI to run correctly as the root user inside a container.
# These settings are standard for containerized HPC environments.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gcc \

    make \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create and set a temporary working directory for compiling the application and its dependencies.
WORKDIR /tmp/build

# Download, build, and install METIS 4.0.3 from source.
# This version requires specific compiler flags and manual installation of the library and header
# to a system-wide location (/usr/local) so that other builds (like MFEM) can find it.

    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make CFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC' OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp metis.h /usr/local/include/

# Download, build, and install Hypre 2.28.0 from source.
# It is configured with specific flags to disable Fortran and enable 64-bit integer support.
# The configure script automatically detects the system's MPI installation.
RUN wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install

# The 'parallel' make target builds the library with MPI support enabled. The build system
# will automatically find the previously installed METIS and Hypre dependencies in /usr/local.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc)

# Clone and build the Laghos application.
# The build is linked against the MFEM library compiled in the previous step.

    cd Laghos && \
    MFEM_DIR=/tmp/build/mfem make -j$(nproc)

# copying the Laghos executable to a location on the system's PATH, and moving the necessary
# input data files. The temporary build directory is then removed to keep the final image clean.
RUN mkdir -p /app && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/data/* /app/ && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build

# Set environment variables required for OpenMPI to run correctly as the root user inside a container.
# These settings are standard for containerized HPC environments.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

# FIX: Manually copy the library and all required header files to system paths. The standard
# 'make install' is unreliable and fails to copy all necessary headers, causing downstream build failures.
RUN wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzvf hypre-v2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp lib/libHYPRE.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/

# Clone and build the MFEM (Modular Finite Element Methods) library version 4.7 from source.
# Explicitly provide paths to the system-installed Hypre and METIS dependencies,
# as the MFEM Makefile does not automatically detect them in /usr/local.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local

# Clone and build the Laghos application.
# The build is linked against the MFEM library compiled in the previous step.
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    MFEM_DIR=/tmp/build/mfem make -j$(nproc)

# Prepare the final application environment. This includes creating a dedicated app directory,
# copying the Laghos executable to a location on the system's PATH, and moving the necessary
# input data files. The temporary build directory is then removed to keep the final image clean.
RUN mkdir -p /app && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos && \
    cp /tmp/build/Laghos/data/* /app/ && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build

# Set environment variables required for OpenMPI to run correctly as the root user inside a container.
# These settings are standard for containerized HPC environments.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

This attempt hypothesizes that the workload may perform better on an x86_64 architecture. I am switching to a high core-count AMD instance (c7a.12xlarge) and matching the number of tasks to the 48 available vCPUs for optimal 1:1 rank-to-core mapping.

The previous ARM-based run (118.2 on hpc7g.16xlarge) significantly outperformed the AMD run (98.4 on c7a.12xlarge). This suggests the application is better optimized for the Graviton3 architecture. This attempt will test another 64-core Graviton3 instance (m7g.16xlarge) which has double the memory. This will help determine if the application is memory-bandwidth limited, which could lead to a performance improvement over the previous best score.

The m7g.16xlarge (ARM Graviton3) instance provided the best performance (132.5), suggesting the application benefits from its architecture and high memory capacity/bandwidth. To further optimize, this attempt keeps the best-performing hardware and tunes the application itself by increasing the polynomial order to 4 ('-o 4'). This increases the problem's computational intensity and total degrees of freedom, which could lead to a higher overall performance rate.

The third attempt on the `m7g.16xlarge` (ARM Graviton3) instance achieved the highest performance score of 132.5. A subsequent attempt to tune application parameters (`-o 4`) on this optimal hardware resulted in a significant performance decrease to 113.5. This indicates that the peak performance for this workload has been found, and further iterations are unlikely to yield improvement.

manager.name: Build and Deploy Laghos

context.details:
Build laghos, building hyre, metis, and mfem from source first. 
You MUST install hypre 2.28.0 and disable fortran and add the --enable-bigint flag.
You MUST install metis 4.0.3 from https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz and add OPTFLAGS=-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration.
You MUST install mfem 4.7 and make parallel.
You MUST ensure all globbed files from ./data from the root of the laghos codebase are in the WORKDIR.

context.optimize: Run cube_311_hex.mesh with laghos in the pwd. You MUST maximize the Major kernels total rate (megadofs x time steps / second). You can add additional parameters to achieve that goal.
